centralVerdict: CapabilityOutcomeSurface is not a directly observed Game object. It is a probe-relative research model whose only warranted claims are the surface properties identified under an explicit observation/intervention design; unresolved alternatives remain an equivalence class.

reconstructions.from: CapabilityOutcomeSurface as if latent truth object
reconstructions.reason: finite observational/probe data generally underdetermine the latent response relation
threshold is identifiable only relative to declared capability coordinates, criterion, model assumptions and probes
gradient/sensitivity is local, coordinate-dependent and can be confounded by latent heterogeneity/chance without repeated/interventional probes
observational residuals do not identify whether variation is RNG, hidden state, teammate/opponent behavior, system automation or unmodeled capability
authoritative recovery transitions can be structurally known, but severity/cost aggregation requires an evaluation/query

researchContracts.name: ChallengeObservationDesign
researchContracts.definition: Declares observed variables, sampling population/policy family, repeated-trial structure, seeds/exogenous controls, capability proxies, opponent distributions, assistance/mapping conditions, history state and censoring/selection rules.

researchContracts.name: ChallengeInterventionSet
researchContracts.definition: Exact ProbeTransformations deliberately applied to capability expression, mapping/assist, opponent policy, exogenous seed/process, evaluation criterion, history/knowledge, or recovery transition while other dimensions are held fixed as far as claimed.

researchContracts.name: IdentifiedChallengeClaim
researchContracts.definition: A challenge property warranted invariantly across all model members consistent with the current observation+intervention evidence and declared assumptions.

researchContracts.name: ChallengeEquivalenceClass
researchContracts.definition: The set of distinct latent response/recovery explanations still observationally/interventionally indistinguishable under the current evidence design.

researchContracts.name: IdentificationStatus
researchContracts.definition: Epistemic status attached to each threshold/discrimination/feasibility/attribution/recovery claim.

minimumProbeFamilies.name: StructuralReachabilityProbe
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: feasibility/infeasibility under an exact complete-enough transition/action/horizon model
minimumProbeFamilies.cannotIdentify: Human difficulty, learning, stochastic support omitted by the structural model

minimumProbeFamilies.name: ControlledCapabilitySweep
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: response differences across known/constructed capability-policy probes and approximate threshold/discrimination along intervened directions
minimumProbeFamilies.cannotIdentify: unprobed SkillProfile dimensions or Human equivalence to synthetic controllers

minimumProbeFamilies.name: RepeatedSameControllerSeedSweep
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: within-controller/exogenous outcome variability under fixed controller and condition
minimumProbeFamilies.cannotIdentify: source label of variance unless seeds/process are actually controlled/observed

minimumProbeFamilies.name: MappingAssistIntervention
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: causal shift/flatten/relocation of response claims attributable to exact assist/mapping transformation
minimumProbeFamilies.cannotIdentify: PlayerValue or independent learning without separate evidence

minimumProbeFamilies.name: OpponentCrossPlayMatrix
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: pairwise/multi-controller interaction response across controlled opponent policies/profiles
minimumProbeFamilies.cannotIdentify: all strategic adaptation from a sparse opponent sample

minimumProbeFamilies.name: HistoryKnowledgeIntervention
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: causal effect of retained/introduced knowledge/history on current response relation
minimumProbeFamilies.cannotIdentify: lower Human memory mechanism by Game data alone

minimumProbeFamilies.name: RecoveryTransitionIntervention
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: authoritative continuation/retry/history/resource consequences of alternate recovery rules

minimumProbeFamilies.name: PopulationTransportAudit
minimumProbeFamilies.identifies: whether aggregate pass-rate differences survive standardization/reweighting across observed capability/history strata
minimumProbeFamilies.cannotIdentify: latent unobserved selection without stronger assumptions/interventions

identifiabilityLaws: AggregatePassRate does not identify a unique challenge response relation
SameAggregateOutcome can arise from different response surfaces and/or different participant populations
ObservedVariance != SkillIndependentRandomness without repeated/controlled attribution probes
Absolute capability location/scale is not identified without a reference/gauge convention in many response models
Threshold and discrimination claims are coordinate-, criterion-, scope- and model-relative
One average assistance effect cannot distinguish threshold shift from flattening or dimension relocation
Synthetic-agent evidence identifies properties of the probed policy family, not Human SkillProfile by identity
Structural infeasibility may be proven without player samples only relative to a sufficiently complete action/transition/horizon model
ObservedPerformance may be nonmonotonic even when attainable capability envelope is monotonic under nested action/policy options
Population pass rate is a convolution/projection of challenge relation and selected population/history distribution
Opponent effects require controlled opponent distributions or cross-play; adaptive opponents are not interchangeable with IID noise
Recovery transitions can be structurally identified while recovery severity remains query/value-relative
Unidentified alternative explanations must remain explicit rather than being collapsed into a fitted parameter story

multidimensionalResults.result: different timing/strategy SkillProfiles can produce identical outcome probability; a single scalar ability ordering is not identified by outcome alone
the same point can have high sensitivity along timing and low sensitivity along strategy or vice versa; discrimination is directional in SkillProfile space
higher latent capability with a changed/riskier selected policy can yield worse observed outcome, so observed performance monotonicity is not a capability law

if higher capability strictly contains lower-capability admissible policy options under the same evaluation and conditions, best-attainable performance cannot worsen; this is an option-set property, not an empirical average-performance guarantee

populationResults.result: a steep skill-sensitive surface under a symmetric mixed population and a flat 50% chance surface can both produce 50% aggregate pass rate
a structurally harder/high-threshold level reached only by selected experts can show a higher observed pass rate than an easier level faced by a broad novice-heavy population
reweighting both levels to a shared capability distribution can reverse the naive aggregate comparison, showing pass-rate difficulty is population-bound

assistanceResults.result: different assistance transformations can be parameterized to produce the same mean success gain at one sampled population while having different low/mid/high capability effects
matched assistance evaluation across multiple controlled capability probes distinguishes approximate threshold shift, flattening and dimension relocation

opponentResults.result: same average win rate can arise from different matchup matrices; pairwise cross-play is needed to expose nontransitive or opponent-specific challenge structure
changing a strategic opponent policy conditionally changes response to target policy; seed-noise averaging cannot substitute for opponent intervention

recoveryVerdict.reason: Game authority can often enumerate exact post-outcome transitions and preserved/lost state directly; any scalar severity combines heterogeneous time/resource/history/social/opportunity costs and belongs to a declared evaluation query

externalAnchors.pressure: IRT models themselves exhibit translation/scale and higher-parameter identifiability problems; latent location/slope/guessing parameters are not automatically unique from response data

distinct latent causal models can be observationally indistinguishable and interventions are necessary for identifiability under the studied setting; motivates explicit intervention/equivalence-class discipline without importing the theorem universally
level difficulty/churn predictions improve when evolving population skill/persistence selection is modeled, supporting population-pass-rate separation
AI policy performance can correlate with human completion even without matching human absolute ability; synthetic policies provide structural probes but not Human identity
game difficulty and haptic assistance can be independently manipulated, supporting intervention-based separation of task-side and capability-expression-side effects
different assistance techniques target different core tasks and can alter performance/challenge through different mechanisms, opposing one-dimensional assist=difficulty assumptions

N0: latent response models have identifiability/gauge issues; interventions can distinguish otherwise equivalent latent explanations in defined causal settings; game pass-rate models are population dependent; assistance dimensions can be independently manipulated

foundationReopen.reason: C tightens epistemic status of downstream challenge models and consumes frozen ProbeTransformation/provenance rather than contradicting semantic/action foundations.
